component.name: Gearbench
component.summary: Settings for Logitech G keyboards and mice, the G432 headset and the Astro A50 Gen 4

description.p: Gearbench is a control panel for Logitech G keyboards (the G915, G915 TKL, G815, G515 TKL and G515 LIGHTSPEED TKL), mice (the G502 X PLUS, G502 X, G502 X LIGHTSPEED, G502 X PLUS MILLENNIUM FALCON, G502 HERO, G502 LIGHTSPEED, G305, PRO X SUPERLIGHT, PRO WIRELESS and G903 LIGHTSPEED HERO) and the G432 headset, and for the Astro A50 Gen 4 headset with its base station's switch on PC. Only these models attach, the A50's Xbox edition not among them; the G913 TKL and G813 share the G915 TKL's and G815's ids and attach as those. The models not yet checked on the hardware are trials: the G515 LIGHTSPEED TKL, G915 TKL and G815 keyboards and the G502 X, G502 X LIGHTSPEED, G502 X PLUS MILLENNIUM FALCON, G502 LIGHTSPEED, PRO X SUPERLIGHT, PRO WIRELESS and G903 LIGHTSPEED HERO mice. On a mouse other than the G502 X PLUS, G305 and G502 HERO, Gearbench writes nothing to the onboard profile until that is tested on the hardware. It talks to the keyboards, the mice and the G432 over their vendor HID++ 2.0 interfaces, on a cable or through a LIGHTSPEED receiver, and to the A50's base station over its own vendor HID interface, with no vendor software and nothing running as root. For each device it shows only what that device can do.

ul.li: Per-key and zone lighting, with the six effects the firmware has
G1 to G5 on the G915 and G815, and F1 to F12 on the G915 TKL, bound to key combinations or macros, on the base layer and, from gearbench-ctl, the MR shift layer
Three M profiles, switched from the window, by the M1 to M3 keys, or, on a keyboard without them, from the tray's menu
Backlight brightness, snapped to a level the firmware keeps
DPI set live and remembered per model; the onboard DPI stage list and report rate rewritten on the G502 X PLUS and G305, and on the other mice the report rate set live in host mode
On each mouse but the G305, those of G4 to G9 it has, bound to key combinations, macros, DPI shift, DPI up, down or cycle, or the browser buttons, each model's on its own
Lighting where the mouse has it, either its own or following the keyboard
On the A50, microphone level, sidetone, noise gate and mic EQ
The A50's three EQ presets, edited band by band or imported from Astro Command Center's files
The A50's stream port mix, its base station's own settings and its battery
On the A50, changes apply at once; Save writes them to the base station's flash, and until then Revert to saved undoes all of them but Auto shut-off and which preset is active
The A50's Game and Chat as two outputs, and Gearbench Spatial, a 7.1 output for games on the A50 or the G432, rendered for headphones from measured heads
On the G432, sidetone, noise suppression for its microphone, and Logitech G432 Equalizer, an output whose presets are edited band by band or copied from the A50's

description.p: Game profiles hold a lighting and binding set that loads itself while a named program's window has focus, and macros are recorded from the Macros tab and replayed through a uinput virtual keyboard and mouse.

Lighting is volatile and the keyboard's onboard profile is never written. Each write to the mouse's onboard profile, from the window or gearbench-ctl, backs up every profile sector first and reads the written sector back after.

New devices: the G515 TKL keyboard, tested on the hardware; the G502 HERO mouse, its DPI stages written to the mouse; the Logitech G432 headset, with its sidetone, an equalizer, noise suppression and spatial sound; and, as trials not yet checked on the hardware, the G515 LIGHTSPEED TKL, G915 TKL and G815 keyboards and seven more mice. The A50 keeps up to 16 presets of your own.
The app id and the spatial output are renamed: log out and back in once, and change each game's launch option to PULSE_SINK=gearbench-spatial %command%.
